name: Rock Eagle Effigy Mound
unique: A bird effigy built of quartz rock with a 120 foot wingspan, made by people who left no written record, sitting in the woods beside a 4-H camp that has protected it by accident.
buzz: You climb a tower to see the shape, which is the only way to understand it. Nobody knows which bird it is or why it was built.

name: Uncle Remus Museum
unique: A museum in two restored slave cabins about Joel Chandler Harris and the Brer Rabbit stories, told with the complexity the material now demands rather than as a children's display.
buzz: Small and dated in places, and worth it for the original editions and the honest conversation about where the stories came from. Cheap and quiet.

name: Alice Walker Driving Tour
unique: A self guided route through the Eatonton of Alice Walker's childhood, past the church, the school and the houses that turn up in her essays about growing up poor and Black in middle Georgia.
buzz: The map is free from the visitor center and the stops are ordinary buildings with extraordinary provenance. Read The Color Purple first.

name: Lake Oconee
unique: Nineteen thousand acres of lake on the Oconee with 370 miles of shoreline, built for power and turned into the weekend water of Atlanta an hour away.
buzz: The lake is the point and the marinas rent. Summer weekends are busy with wake boats, and the fishing is better in winter.

name: Eatonton Courthouse Square
unique: A courthouse square in the town that produced two of Georgia's major writers a generation apart, with the old commercial block and a dairy festival that still runs in June.
buzz: The square is small and the literary connection is the draw. The June dairy festival fills it once a year.

name: Jarrell Plantation State Historic Site
customer: Farm history people, families, school groups
unique: A working farm complex held by one family from 1847 into the 1970s, with the original house, a steam powered gin, a sawmill and a syrup mill still in their sheds.
buzz: The machines are the surprise, a whole self sufficient operation with its own power. The family kept everything, which is why it survived.

name: Juliette and the Whistle Stop Cafe
customer: Film people, families, fried green tomato fans
unique: A mill village that became the setting for Fried Green Tomatoes, with the cafe from the film still serving fried green tomatoes and the old grist mill standing over the Ocmulgee.
buzz: The tomatoes are the order and the mill is the photograph. It gets busy on weekends with Atlanta day trippers.

name: Ocmulgee River at Juliette
unique: Wide water below the mill with sandbars and a shoal, part of the Ocmulgee water trail, and good bank access right behind the cafe.
buzz: An easy paddle with the mill as a landmark. Bank fishing for catfish is a local evening habit.

name: Monticello Downtown
unique: A courthouse square with a ring of shops and a historic residential grid, in a county named for a man who never came and a town named for his house.
buzz: Small and tidy with a couple of good shops. A useful stop between Athens and Macon.

name: Jasper County Wildlife and Farm Land
unique: Pine and hardwood ridges between the Ocmulgee and the Oconee with public land, hunting seasons, and more than fifty bird species recorded on the county checklists.
buzz: Deer and turkey hunting is the main draw and the land takes pressure well. Birders work the edges in spring.

name: Lloyd Shoals Dam and Lake
unique: A 1910 hydroelectric dam on the Ocmulgee that drowned the shoals the town was built around, with the lake behind it and the old power architecture still in place.
buzz: The dam is the interesting structure and the lake is quiet. Access is limited, so check before planning a launch.

name: Sparta Courthouse Square
unique: A square in a town laid out in 1795 with roughly six hundred historic structures in the county, from antebellum houses to the commercial block that burned and rebuilt.
buzz: The density of old buildings for a town this size is the surprise. Walk the side streets, the square is only the start.

name: Lake Sinclair at Hancock
unique: Fifteen thousand acres of lake on the Oconee with a long wooded shoreline on the Hancock side, public ramps and water warm enough to swim from May to September.
buzz: Cheaper and quieter than Lake Oconee next door, with good crappie fishing in the timber.

name: Hancock County Historic Sites
unique: A county with hundreds of recorded historic sites from Native American, European and African American settlement, including plantation remains, churches and a Black landowning history that survived Reconstruction.
buzz: Best done with the county's site list in hand, since much of it is unmarked. The churches and cemeteries are the most moving stops.

name: A.H. Stephens State Park
unique: Liberty Hall, the home of Confederate vice president Alexander Stephens, preserved with his books and furniture, inside a state park with a lake, cottages and a CCC built recreation hall.
buzz: The house is the reason to come and the museum does not soften Stephens. Camping and the lake make it a full day for families.

name: Crawfordville Film Locations
unique: A county seat so intact that productions keep using it as a stand in for other southern towns, with the courthouse, storefronts and houses appearing in films and series.
buzz: Locals can list what was shot where. The square is the set and it is still a working town.

name: Taliaferro County Farm Roads
unique: One of the poorest and least changed counties in Georgia, with tenant houses, churches and cotton fields that look like a documentary about the 1930s.
buzz: Photographers come for exactly this. Be respectful, people live here and the poverty is not scenery to them.

name: Callaway Plantation
customer: History travellers, architecture people, school groups
unique: A plantation complex with a 1790s log cabin, a Greek Revival house, a slave cabin, a school and a country store, showing two hundred years of one county's farm life in one yard.
buzz: The range of buildings in one place is what makes it, from the log cabin to the store. Self guided and cheap.

name: Washington Historic District
unique: A grid of streets laid out in 1780 with one of the largest concentrations of pre 1860 buildings in Georgia, including the 1784 Heard House and a courthouse by the same architect as the state capitol.
buzz: The whole town is the museum and it is free. The walking tour takes a half day and the houses are lived in.

name: Little River Water Trail
unique: A designated paddling trail on the Little River through Wilkes and Lincoln counties, with shoals, granite outcrops and boat ramps marked along the way.
buzz: Good beginner water with clear signs and a shuttle map. Spring runs are best before the summer heat.

name: Washington-Wilkes Historical Museum
unique: A county collection covering the Wilkes County gold rush, the Confederate gold legend and the families who built the town, in a house museum a block off the square.
buzz: The gold rush material is the surprise, Georgia had one before California. Ask about the legend, the volunteers enjoy telling it.

name: Elijah Clark State Park
unique: A park on Clarks Hill Lake with a beach, a boat ramp and campsites on a point, named for a Revolutionary soldier whose grave and reconstructed homestead are on the grounds.
buzz: The lakeside sites are the ones to book and the water is the whole point. The homestead is small and easy to walk past.

name: Clarks Hill Lake
unique: Seventy thousand acres of Corps lake on the Savannah River with 1,200 miles of shoreline, standing timber and coves that stay quiet even in summer.
buzz: Big water with good striper and largemouth fishing. The Georgia side is less developed than South Carolina's.

name: Lincoln County Courthouse and Lincolnton Square
unique: A courthouse square in a county named for a general, on land that was once the frontier with the Creek Nation, twenty minutes from the lake.
buzz: Small and quiet, with the lake traffic passing through. A quick look on the way to Elijah Clark.

name: Belle Meade Hunt
unique: A traditional fox hunt opening the season with riders in pink, hounds in the square and a blessing of the hounds, staged for the town before the field moves off.
buzz: The opening meet is a spectacle and the whole town turns out. Arrive early for a spot on the square.

name: Blind Willie McTell Memorial
unique: The grave and memorial of Blind Willie McTell, the twelve string bluesman who recorded Statesboro Blues and whose song about him Bob Dylan never finished.
buzz: Blues people make the trip and the town holds a festival in his name. The grave is quiet and easy to find.

name: Thomson Downtown
unique: A railroad town main street with a handful of good local restaurants and shops, close enough to Augusta to be an easy evening out.
buzz: The local places on the main street are the draw and they are cheap. Half an hour covers the walk.

name: Mistletoe State Park
unique: A wooded park on a peninsula of Clarks Hill Lake with a beach, a boat ramp and campsites within sight of the water, twenty five minutes from Augusta.
buzz: The closest real lake camping to Augusta and it books out in summer. The beach is the family draw.

name: Savannah Rapids Park and Canal Headgates
unique: The headgates where the Augusta Canal takes water from the Savannah River, with the 1845 gate structure still controlling the flow and a trail that begins the canal towpath into the city.
buzz: The rapids and the gates are the view and the towpath is flat and shaded. It is the start of the best bike ride in the area.

name: Euchee Creek Greenway
unique: A paved greenway following a creek through Columbia County's parks, with boardwalks over the floodplain and connections toward the canal trail.
buzz: Flat, shaded and well used by locals. Good early morning ride or run.
